how_this_file_is_used: scripts/supply-chain-gate.mjs re-runs both audits against the current lockfiles on every verification run. A cargo finding whose package is absent from `cargo tree --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --edges normal,build` is classified mechanically and needs no entry here. Everything else must be listed below with a reachability argument and a review date. An unlisted finding fails the gate; a listed finding whose review_by has passed fails the gate. Acknowledgements expire on purpose - the alternative is a permanent excuse.

npm.shipped_artifact: The Compy installer contains the Rust executable and the Vite build output (tauri.conf.json build.frontendDist = ../dist). bundle.resources and bundle.externalBin are unset, so no node_modules content is packaged. Every npm advisory below is therefore a build-integrity or developer-workstation concern, not a concern for an installed copy of Compy - which is a reachability statement, not a dismissal: a compromised build tool would reach the installer through dist/.

postcss.why: Path traversal in PostCSS source-map auto-loading. Reached through vite (the frontend build) and the shadcn CLI. It processes only this repository's own CSS during a local build; no attacker-controlled source map is ever fed to it, and postcss ships nothing into the installer.

esbuild.why: The advisory is against the esbuild development server, which allows any website to read responses from it. Compy's build runs `vite build`, not a served dev bundle exposed to a browsing session, and esbuild is not in the installer.

fast-uri.why: Host confusion via literal backslashes, reached only through ajv inside the @modelcontextprotocol/sdk that the shadcn developer CLI depends on. It is never executed by the frontend build or by Compy at runtime.

brace-expansion.why: Denial of service via unbounded expansion, reached only through minimatch inside ts-morph inside the shadcn developer CLI. Not executed by the build, not in the installer.

@hono/node-server.why: Path traversal in serve-static. Reached only through the MCP SDK that the shadcn developer CLI depends on; Compy runs no Hono server and ships none.

@modelcontextprotocol/sdk.why: Listed because it depends on the vulnerable @hono/node-server range above. Same path, same reasoning: developer CLI only.

cargo.note: Compy's own Rust source references none of these crates: a repository-wide search for quick_xml, crossbeam, rayon, anyhow and downcast_mut across src-tauri/**/*.rs and the manifests returns nothing. Every entry below arrives transitively through Tauri.

RUSTSEC-2026-0194.why: Quadratic run time when checking a start tag for duplicate attribute names - a denial of service that needs attacker-controlled XML. Both copies in the Windows build parse XML that Compy or Tauri generates: 0.37.5 through tauri-winrt-notification (toast XML the notification plugin builds itself) and 0.39.4 through plist inside tauri-utils (bundle metadata handled at build and codegen time). No user, network, or game-supplied XML reaches either. Patched at >=0.41.0, which is a Tauri-side upgrade, not ours.

RUSTSEC-2026-0195.why: Unbounded namespace-declaration allocation in NsReader, memory-exhaustion denial of service. Same two paths and the same reasoning as RUSTSEC-2026-0194: the XML is ours, not an attacker's.

RUSTSEC-2026-0204.why: Invalid pointer dereference in the fmt::Pointer impl for Atomic and Shared. Triggering it requires formatting one of those types with {:p} while the underlying pointer is invalid. crossbeam-epoch reaches the build only through crossbeam-deque <- rayon-core; Compy declares no dependency on rayon or crossbeam and never names either type, so no Compy code can reach the formatting path.

RUSTSEC-2026-0190.why: Unsoundness in Error::downcast_mut(). Compy calls downcast_mut nowhere, and anyhow arrives through tauri-build, tauri-plugin and tauri-utils - predominantly build dependencies. No known exploit path, no vulnerability rating.

RUSTSEC-2025-0081.why: Unmaintained, with no advisory of a defect. Reaches the build through urlpattern <- tauri-utils. Retiring it is a Tauri-side change; it is tracked here so the warning cannot quietly become a vulnerability without a re-review.

RUSTSEC-2025-0075.why: Unmaintained, no known defect. Same urlpattern <- tauri-utils path as the rest of the unic family.
